pending_commit.commit_message: UPSTREAM: USB: add usbfs ioctl to retrieve the connection speed The usbfs interface does not provide any way for the user to learn the speed at which a device is connected. The current API includes a USBDEVFS_CONNECTINFO ioctl, but all it provides is the device's address and a one-bit value indicating whether the connection is low speed. That may have sufficed in the era of USB-1.1, but it isn't good enough today. This patch introduces a new ioctl, USBDEVFS_GET_SPEED, which returns a numeric value indicating the speed of the connection: unknown, low, full, high, wireless, super, or super-plus. Similar information (not exactly the same) is available through sysfs, but it seems reasonable to provide the actual value in usbfs. Signed-off-by: Alan Stern <stern@rowland.harvard.edu> Reported-by: Reinhard Huck <reinhard.huck@thesycon.de> Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org> BUG=b:133773289 TEST=Build and boot (cherry picked from commit c01b244ad848ac7f0faa141182db80650a8a761a) Signed-off-by: Dmitry Torokhov <dtor@chromium.org> Change-Id: I898af5a1af8f7ed1b2397efbd95e0c96c0bbe7a3 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1651155 Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Guenter Roeck <groeck@chromium.org>

FROMLIST: USB: add usbfs ioctl to retrieve the connection parameters Recently usfbs gained availability to retrieve device speed, but there is sill no way to determine the bus number or list of ports the device is connected to when using usbfs. While this information can be obtained from sysfs, not all environments allow sysfs access. In a jailed environment a program might be simply given an opened file descriptor to usbfs device, and it is really important that all data can be gathered from said file descriptor. This patch introduces a new ioctl, USBDEVFS_CONNINFO_EX, which return extended connection information for the device, including the bus number, address, port list and speed. The API allows kernel to extend amount of data returned by the ioctl and userspace has an option of adjusting the amount of data it is willing to consume. A new capability, USBDEVFS_CAP_CONNINFO_EX, is introduced to help userspace in determining whether the kernel supports this new ioctl. Signed-off-by: Dmitry Torokhov <dmitry.torokhov@gmail.com> BUG=b:133773289 TEST=Build and boot (am from https://patchwork.kernel.org/patch/10985613/) Signed-off-by: Dmitry Torokhov <dtor@chromium.org> Change-Id: Ibab3731f48d5faad4177126445f5802d9b2ac6b6 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1651156 Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Guenter Roeck <groeck@chromium.org>

cros-kernel2.eclass: Skip Image.gz creation for arm64 On arm64 kernels we compress the kernel in this eclass (see _cros-kernel2_compress_fit_kernel() for more info). The default target of the kernel build compresses the kernel with gzip, and that just wastes some time during the build. Only build the Image and dtbs targets so we can avoid this small overhead. UPSTREAM: drm/rockchip: Add implicit fencing support for planes Render like lima will attach a fence to the framebuffer dma_buf, so the display driver should wait for it to finish before showing the framebufferto prevent tearing. Generally tested on rk3188, rk3288, rk3328 and rk3399 and together with an actual lima-based kmscube on rk3188 and rk3328.
